sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from $23.7 billion in FY2016 to $51.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F168], but the table mixes recast revenue with the first-reported figures, whose FY2025 value is $58.9 billion [X10], so growth rates here are indicative only.
The shape is cyclical: revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 [D161], rose 153.2% in FY2021 [D200] and 76.5% to $61.0 billion in FY2022 [D238][F7].
The FY2022 jump came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher volumes from the Shell Permian acquisition, and sales and other operating revenues rose $32,666 million [P59].
FY2017 was a loss year, with a net loss of $855 million [F12] and impairment charges of $6,601 million [X113], including $2.5 billion after tax on the San Juan Basin and Barnett [P80].
Revenue fell 20.5% to $48.5 billion in FY2023 [D274][F8] because lower realized commodity prices outweighed higher sales volumes, and sales and other operating revenues fell $22,353 million [P47].
Crude oil's share of revenue rose from 40.7% in FY2017 [D529] to 66.3% in FY2025 [D551], but it added only 0.1pp to FY2025 growth [D553].
Revenue grew 4.9% in FY2025 [D342], with Lower 48 contributing 8.0pp [D713] on a 70.2% revenue share [D711] and natural gas adding 4.4pp [D586].
Sales and other operating revenues rose $4,199 million, as higher volumes of $6,197 million, including Marathon Oil, outweighed $4,615 million of lower realized crude prices [P28].
Operating leverage was negative: cost of revenue grew 11.6% [D352] against revenue growth of 4.9% [D342], and net income fell 13.6% [D343].
Basic EPS fell 18.7% [D344], more than net income's 13.6% decline [D343], because the diluted share count rose 6.1% to 1,253.4 million [D356][X131]; the filings cited do not explain the increase.
The pack has no operating income line, so net margin is the guide: 15.4% in FY2025 [F30] against a window median of 17.9% [D831], a high of 30.6% [D830] and a low of -19.8% [D829].
That still ranks at the 83rd percentile of six energy peers, whose median is 8.1% [D846][D847].
Cost of revenue rose to 37.9% of revenue from 36.6% [D326][D292], and D&A rose to 19.5% from 17.5% [D330][D296].
DD&A increased $1,901 million, mainly from the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22].
SG&A fell to 1.5% of revenue from 2.1% [D328][D294] because FY2024 carried $545 million of Marathon transaction expenses [P23].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9% from 32.4% [D332][D298], and earnings in Other fell $366 million, mainly from the absence of a $455 million tax benefit [P8].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025 [F59][D333], up from 2.18x in FY2024 [D299], with operating cash flow at 33.6% of revenue [D331].
Operating cash flow slipped from $20.1 billion because lower commodity prices were mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [F58][P6].
Capex and free cash flow lines stop at FY2022 in the pack, so current capital intensity cannot be measured; the FY2018 to FY2022 free-cash-flow-to-net-income median was 0.98x [D840].
The pack shows net cash of $7.1 billion in FY2025, up from $6.1 billion [D337][D303], and the 100th percentile among six energy peers, whose median is -7.7% of revenue [D850][D851].
That net cash rests on total debt of $1.0 billion [D336], which matches the current portion alone [X203]; long-term debt is untagged after FY2020, when it was $19.1 billion [F157].
Net cash and its peer rank are therefore unreliable, and I draw no conclusion from them [D337][D850].
In 2025 the company spent $5.0 billion on buybacks, $4.0 billion on dividends and $0.9 billion on debt retirement [P7].
Buybacks and dividends totalled $9.0 billion [D339], 46% of operating cash flow [P31], yet the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D356].
Return on average equity of 12.4% sits at the 33rd percentile, below the peer median of 14.9% [D341][D852][D853].
Data quality [R1]: FY2025 revenue is $51.8 billion in the table against $58.9 billion in that year's 10-K [F10][X10], so margins and growth mix two presentations.
Earnings erosion: net income fell from $18.7 billion in FY2022 to $8.0 billion in FY2025 [F17][F20], a 3-year CAGR of -24.7% [D845].
Lower realized crude prices cut FY2025 revenue by $4,615 million [P28].
Three straight years of decline [D275][D309][D343] show earnings still tracking prices rather than the volume added by acquisitions.
Rising fixed charges: interest expense reached $1,176 million against $941 million [X81][X80], driven by debt assumed with Marathon Oil [P10].
Higher D&A and interest raise the breakeven price [D330][X81].
Net margin at or above the window median of 17.9% [D831] would confirm stabilisation, while a reading below the FY2025 level of 15.4% [F30] would extend the decline; both appear in the FY2026 10-K.
Operating cash flow to net income falling below the FY2024 level of 2.18x [D299], from 2.48x [D333], would show earnings catching up with cash; check the FY2026 10-K.
A diluted share count below the FY2024 level of 1,180.9 million [X130], from 1,253.4 million [X131], would show buybacks outrunning issuance in the FY2026 10-K.
Disposition proceeds of less than the $5 billion target [P32], against $3.2 billion completed in 2025 [P32], would mean the FY2026 10-K shows a miss.
